  • other (adjective): 'Other' means different or additional. 'Shirts that fit other suit you have' is incorrect because 'other' is usually used with plural nouns or with 'another' for singular.
  • many (determiner): 'Many' means a large number of. 'Shirts that fit many suit you have' is incorrect because 'many' should be used with plural nouns ('many suits you have').
Related structure or vocabulary: any + singular/plural noun: used to refer to one, some, or every thing or person in a group

The phrase 'did not notice ____ differences' suggests a negative context, so we need a word that works with negatives. In English, 'any' is commonly used in negative sentences to refer to an indefinite quantity or number. The other options do not fit grammatically or semantically.
  • any (determiner): 'Any' is used in negative sentences and questions to refer to an indefinite quantity or number. It fits naturally after 'did not notice' and before the plural noun 'differences.'
  • no (determiner): 'No' is used to make a sentence negative, but since the sentence already has 'did not,' using 'no' would create a double negative, which is incorrect in standard English.
  • much (determiner/quantifier): 'Much' is used with uncountable nouns, but 'differences' is a countable noun, so 'much' is not appropriate here.
  • a (article): 'A' is an indefinite article used with singular countable nouns, but 'differences' is plural, so 'a' cannot be used.
Related structure or vocabulary: In negative sentences, 'any' is used before plural or uncountable nouns to indicate an indefinite amount or number. Structure: not + any + plural/uncountable noun.

The blank requires a word that refers to the whole island being affected by the storm, and then a comparison with the remaining parts. 'All' is used to refer to the entire group collectively, and 'the others' or 'the rest' is used to refer to the remaining parts. However, the correct phrase is 'the rest' when talking about the remaining parts of a singular noun like 'the island.' So, the correct answer is 'All – the rest.'
  • Every – the rest (determiner – noun phrase): 'Every' is used with singular countable nouns and refers to each individual item in a group, not the group as a whole. 'The rest' is correct for the second blank, but 'every' does not fit with 'of the island.'
  • Each – others (determiner – pronoun): 'Each' is used for individual items, not for the whole group. 'Others' is plural and refers to other people or things, but does not fit the context of comparing parts of the island.
  • None – the other (pronoun – pronoun): 'None' means not any, which does not fit the context because the sentence says the island was hit by the storm. 'The other' is used when referring to two items, but here we are talking about more than two parts.
  • All – other (determiner – adjective): 'All' correctly refers to the whole island, but 'other' is not correct here. The correct phrase is 'the rest' when referring to the remaining parts.

In this context, 'no school ... any other' means that all schools are treated equally, with none receiving better equipment or funding than the rest.
  • no – any other (determiner + pronoun): 'No' is used to indicate none of the schools, and 'any other' refers to all the other schools in the district. This structure is commonly used to express equality or lack of exception.
  • a – some other (article + pronoun): 'A' refers to one school, and 'some other' is not a standard comparative structure in this context. It does not clearly express the intended meaning of equality.
  • some – another (determiner + pronoun): 'Some' refers to an unspecified number of schools, and 'another' refers to one more school. This pairing does not fit the context of comparing all schools equally.
  • every – other (determiner + pronoun): 'Every' refers to all schools individually, but 'other' alone is incomplete without 'any' or 'another' to clarify the comparison.
Related structure or vocabulary: Structure: 'No ... any other' is used to compare one member of a group to all others, emphasizing that none is different or superior. Example: 'No student in the class is taller than any other.'
